title: Gas pressure removes a nine-orbit drag stall in one ASASSN-14ko orbit, but other disc models keep stalls
abstract: We test whether a radiation-pressure check at one radius is enough to establish a precessing star-disc drag stall in ASASSN-14ko. We require the orbit to match the 108.44-day period and a proposed apsidal advance, then compute both disc crossings with a steady gas-plus-radiation pressure disc. In one orbit at 0.082 radians per passage, a pure radius^1.5 density law gives a 9.22-orbit interval with absolute energy loss below 0.16 of its maximum. The full disc gives no such interval: its minimum loss is 0.21786 of its maximum, although radiation supplies 77 percent of the pressure at the semi-latus rectum. Other models retain stalls. Of 2932 thin grid models at sampled inclinations of at least 25 degrees, 46 have quiet intervals of at least seven orbits; the longest is 8.70 orbits. Slower and faster precession change this duration. The result is a conditional same-orbit counterexample and a sensitivity survey, not an exclusion of precession or a fit to observed times. Both moving crossing radii must be tested. We include independent numerical checks, original code, synthetic outputs and source hashes.
